source.title: Is Scaling Learned Optimizers Worth It? Evaluating The Value of VeLO's 4000 TPU Months
source.authors: Fady Rezk; Antreas Antoniou; Henry Gouk; Timothy M. Hospedales

record.file_problem: The supplied text includes the paper and appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares adaptive and SGD-family optimizers on benchmark workloads and reports training and validation outcomes that qualify optimizer generalization claims.
record.gate_note: Rows cover fixed-step validation losses for the adaptive optimizers and SGD comparators in Table 2. The paper also reports training losses, time-to-target results, and other metrics; those are not separate rows here because V4 concerns held-out performance. Cited optimizer results are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The ImageNet experiments directly compare held-out performance of adaptive optimizers and momentum SGD, bearing on V4. They use fixed training budgets and default hyperparameters, rather than the version's learning-rate and schedule tuning. The paper's main critique of VeLO does not itself test any listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors question VeLO's claims of being hyperparameter free and providing consistently better and faster optimization on their MLCommons evaluation. These conclusions concern VeLO, rather than a general adaptive-versus-SGD disadvantage.
record.recipe_differences: Independent evaluation of VeLO against MLCommons workloads using a wider set of optimizers and fixed-step or time-to-target protocols; baselines use default hyperparameters rather than the version's specified limited tuning.
record.method_sensitivity: VeLO's total-step prompt (100% versus 75%) changes target attainment and aggregate scores; time-control versus step-control changes the comparison.

fits_no_version.finding: On Criteo, adaptive optimizers have lower validation losses than both momentum-SGD baselines.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer held-out performance comparisons on recommendation workloads.

fits_no_version.finding: On FastMRI, adaptive optimizers have validation losses around 0.2850–0.2851 versus 0.2899 for momentum SGD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer held-out performance comparisons on image reconstruction.

fits_no_version.finding: On OGBG, adaptive optimizers have higher validation losses than momentum SGD, although Appendix E.5 reports higher validation mAP for the adaptive methods.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer rankings on graph prediction depend on the evaluation measure.

fits_no_version.finding: VeLO's step prompt affects target attainment, and VeLO does not consistently outperform handcrafted optimizers in solution quality or training speed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learned optimizer transfer, hyperparameter sensitivity, and efficiency across workloads.

record.problems: The version's stated limited-tuning recipe is not tested: baselines use default hyperparameters. The benchmark covers four workloads and the reported conclusions concern optimizer performance, not memorization or network generalization mechanisms.
record.rows_left_out: Training-loss rows, validation metric rows other than validation loss, VeLO rows, and time/steps-to-target results were left out because the 20 retained rows cover adaptive and SGD-family validation-loss outcomes relevant to V4; see Tables 1–3 and Appendices D–E.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under matched architectures and recipes.
Width scaling beyond zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Learning-rate and schedule tuning; broader tuning; language benchmarks and word-level language models; switching Adam to SGD; an isolated causal test of decoupled weight decay.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout interventions, small-data effects, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its ranking of generalization gaps.
Removal of memorized versus random training examples.

record.verdict_notes: Retained numeric values match Table 2. Classification accuracy and training losses are essential context, but are explicitly declared in rows_left_out, so they are not missing extractions under the supplied rule. Default settings do not establish the outcome after the tuning specified in V4. This study is not an original source for any listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Convolutional versus fully connected image models.

Language benchmarks; broader hyperparameter tuning; decoupled weight decay or switching from Adam to SGD; word-level language models; whether results hold under the specific limited-tuning protocol in the version.
Batch-size effects and adaptive large-batch training recipes.

relationships.condition: ImageNet ResNet-50; default Adam and NAdam versus momentum SGD; 150,000 steps; validation cross-entropy
relationships.reason: R11–R13 and R15 show Adam/NAdam losses of 1.9438/1.9528 versus Heavy Ball/Nesterov 1.6870/1.7022. Table 2 also reports lower adaptive training losses, 0.0470/0.0571 versus 0.2582/0.2512. This supports the loss comparison under defaults.
relationships.display_finding: Adam and NAdam have higher validation cross-entropy despite lower training losses than momentum SGD variants, but accuracy rankings differ.

relation.reason: Its own ImageNet results compare adaptive optimizers with momentum SGD on training and held-out measurements.

tranche.reason: The independent optimizer evaluation supplies paired training and validation comparisons bearing on V4, using fixed budgets and untuned defaults rather than the original learning-rate and schedule tuning. Its critique of VeLO alone does not justify T5 for V4.

source_check.notes: Defaults are the authors' one-shot choices, detailed in Appendix C, without validation-based tuning. The ImageNet loss and accuracy rankings differ; these results cannot establish a metric-independent adaptive-optimizer disadvantage.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Four MLCommons workloads; default optimizer hyperparameters; fixed-step validation-loss comparisons
reader_labels.reason: The authors report that VeLO is not a consistent winner and that different competitors win across workloads and metrics; their evaluation used default baseline settings without HPO, so it does not establish the version's limited-tuning comparison. Rows R1–R20 record the adaptive and SGD comparator validation losses.
